features.statement: Headings are very large, extra-bold, tightly spaced uppercase display type, creating strong hierarchy against small body text.
Uses a single Helvetica-style neo-grotesque sans-serif typeface throughout.
Eyebrow labels above large headings are small, bold, uppercase and letter-spaced.
Read-more and link CTAs are bold uppercase letter-spaced text with an underline.
Palette is warm and saturated: cream, burnt orange, deep teal, forest green, with black accents instead of white and grey.
Announcement bar is solid black with bold white text.
Hero uses a bold CSS gradient background with a large headline and outlined button, instead of a photo.
Visual depth comes only from gradient overlays; no shadows, animations or transforms, and flat square corners.
Feature areas use solid-color or pastel block tiles with text overlays in place of photography.
Card text is left-aligned at the bottom over a dark gradient scrim with underlined link CTAs.
Buttons are outlined rectangular boxes with square corners and bold uppercase text, not filled.
Press section has a dark background with a multi-column grid of quotes and black logos on a white panel.
Newsletter form joins the email input and submit button inline in a single row.
Header shows a visible horizontal text nav bar with a compact script-style logo, positioned below a top gradient band.
Social links in the footer are bold uppercase text labels rather than icons.
Footer has fewer columns, a thin divider above a small mixed-case underlined copyright line.
Layout uses multi-column splits and tile grids built with CSS grid, filling space instead of leaving large empty gaps.
Section titles are promoted to prominent h2 headings, with sub-items as h3 titles.
Press quotes use figure, blockquote and figcaption elements, and form inputs have label elements.
All images have descriptive alt text; payment icons are img elements rather than inline SVGs.
Markup is lean and self-contained: few divs, one style tag, no scripts, hand-written class names.
Page title uses an em-dash tagline format rather than pipe-separated SEO keywords.
